questions.question: Explain how the dopamine reward pathway contributes to addiction.
questions.correctAnswer: The mesolimbic dopamine pathway: addictive substances/behaviours trigger dopamine release in the nucleus accumbens, creating pleasure and reinforcing the behaviour. With repeated use: (1) tolerance develops - more substance needed for same effect; (2) natural rewards produce less pleasure; (3) withdrawal symptoms when substance absent. questions.question: Compare biological and learning theory explanations of addiction.
questions.correctAnswer: Biological: addiction is caused by changes in the dopamine reward pathway (genetic vulnerability, neuroadaptation). Explains physical dependence but ignores why people start using. Learning theory: addiction is maintained by reinforcement (positive = pleasure, negative = withdrawal relief) and conditioned cues. questions.question: Evaluate treatments for addiction, considering both biological and psychological approaches.
questions.correctAnswer: Biological: methadone replaces heroin (reduces withdrawal and craving without the high). Effective for harm reduction but doesn't address psychological dependence. questions.question: Full-Mark Response Evaluate whether biological or learning theory provides a better explanation of addiction. <div class="
questions.correctAnswer: A grade 9 response will: describe biological explanation (dopamine pathway, tolerance, withdrawal, genetics); describe learning explanation (classical conditioning of cues, operant reinforcement); evaluate biological (strong neuroscience evidence but cannot explain why most people who try substances don't become addicted); evaluate learning (explains environmental triggers and maintenance but doesn't explain initial vulnerability); conclude: both are needed - biological factors create vulnerability (not everyone is equally susceptible), learning theory explains how addiction develops and is maintained in specific contexts. A diathesis-stress model combining both provides the most complete explanation.
